title: GPU Blue/Green Scale Operator Terraform module for Private VPC (ASG/Karpenter)
creator: Nina Patel
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module that encapsulates a Blue/Green style operator for GPU node groups in Private VPC deployments. The module should support both ASG-based and Karpenter-based provisioning, expose a single configuration surface for selecting the orchestrator, and include built-in health checks, graceful node draining hooks, and an automated driver/AMI upgrade path. This ticket covers design, implementation, unit/integration test plans, and deployment runbook for the module. Goals: reduce toil when onboarding new GPU workloads to Private, provide safe upgrade patterns, and make health checks actionable via Redwood Console observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Terraform module exposes variables to select orchestrator: 'orchestrator = "asg" | "karpenter"' and validates mutually exclusive settings.
2) Module creates nodegroup resources with recommended defaults for GPU instance types, tagging for ownership and billing, and outputs nodepool identifiers.
3) Health checks: node-level probe (driver/daemonset/gpudiag), continuous heartbeat metric exported to Console, and automatic cordon/drain policy on recurring failures.
4) Upgrade path: support Blue/Green replacement of nodegroups via new launch template/AMI rotation (ASG) or provisioner lifecycle (Karpenter) with minimal disruption and a clear rollback.
5) Integration tests run in a Private staging cluster exercising ASG and Karpenter flows and validate drain hooks, workload rescheduling, and KV cache warm restart for inference containers.
6) Documentation: module README, example usages (ASG and Karpenter), and operational runbook in Confluence linked from the PR.
7) No regression in existing Private deploy pipelines; module passes terraform plan validation and CI linting.
implementation_notes: Design decisions: prefer explicit 'strategy' variable with values ['bluegreen','rolling'] but default to 'bluegreen' for safer upgrades. Provide separate submodules for ASG and Karpenter to keep resource graphs small. Use lifecycle 'create_before_destroy' for ASG LaunchTemplate swaps and Karpenter provisioner 'ttl' tuning to allow drain before termination. Implement a small Lambda (or controller) for health adjudication that marks a node unhealthy after X failed probes and triggers cordon+drain via kube API; make this optional (toggleable) and pluggable for customers with stricter policies. Add tag convention 'redwood:pool=<name>' and outputs 'nodepool_name','nodegroup_arn','provisioner_name'. Ensure all IAM roles are minimal and documented. Prefer new Terraform module namespace 'redwood/gpu-node-operator/private'.
test_plan:
Unit tests: terraform validate/plan for both orchestrator modes and variable edge cases.
Integration tests: deploy to a Private staging VPC with minimal inference workload; steps: 1) create ASG pool and run 100 small inferences to warm KV cache; 2) trigger AMI rotation and verify Blue/Green swap completes within SLO and no lost inferences beyond acceptable window; 3) repeat with Karpenter provisioner and verify node provisioning and drain hooks; 4) simulate driver crash and verify health adjudicator triggers cordon+drain and workloads reschedule.
Observability: assert metrics appear in Console (node_health_down, drain_events) and logs point to controller actions.
CI: include acceptance smoke in 'infra-integration' pipeline that can be gated for merges to main.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge module behind feature flag in Terraform registry and publish pre-release.
2) Smoke deploy to internal staging clusters and run integration tests (ASG & Karpenter).
3) Enable for one non-critical customer tenant in Private (canary). Monitor health metrics and rollback window 48h.
4) Gradually enable across customers after 3 successful canaries.
5) Announce via release notes and update onboarding docs.
rollback_plan:
If regressions are detected (increased inference error rate or unexpected node loss):
- For ASG: revert to previous LaunchTemplate and set desired capacity to previous node count; disable new lifecycle hook; trigger immediate replacement.
- For Karpenter: restore previous provisioner config via Terraform, scale up old pool labels, and reassign workloads.
- In both cases: run diagnostic script to collect kernel/driver logs and GPU daemonset status, escalate to SRE.
- If automated rollback fails, manual remediation runbook triggers with on-call SRE and Platform Eng.

2026-02-25 - Priya Singh (SRE): Suggested adding out-of-band health adjudicator to avoid relying solely on K8s nodeReady - will draft a minimal Lambda controller interface.
2026-03-03 - Marco Rivera: Prototype implemented; uploaded example under examples/karpenter and examples/asg. Running integration tests in staging cluster 'private-stg-03'.

2026-03-08 - QA (Ethan Brooks): Integration test showed intermittent race where launch template swap completed but kube-controller-manager delayed binding pods; mitigation: add pre-drain readiness probe and extend wait window in rollout plan.
